newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EKOKU DOUBLE KEEPS UP WIMBLEDON'S WINNING WAYS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EKOKU DOUBLE KEEPS UP WIMBLEDON'S WINNING WAYS.

text.p: Two goals from Efan Ekoku spurred Wimbledon to their fourth successive win and sixth place in England's premier league on Monday and plunged Southampton deeper into relegation trouble.
It continued a remarkable turnaround for the London club after losing their first three matches of the season and put them on 12 points from seven matches, five adrift of table topping Liverpool.
It also continued Southampton's woeful start to the season, without a win and one place above bottom club Blackburn only on a slim goal difference.
Wimbledon took the lead after 12 minutes when Marcus Gayle took advantage of a poor attempt at a clearance by goalkeeper Dave Beasant to lash a loose ball home.

Southampton failed to exploit a number of chances that came their way and six minutes before half time they found themselves two down when Beasant was again at fault when he allowed Ekoku's shot to squirm under his body.

A casual and totally misdirected back pass from Matthew Le Tissier enabled Ekoku to score his second of the night in the 73rd minute and only Matthew Oakley's late reposte for Southampton prevented them from occupying bottom spot in the table.
